chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Rabi' ibn Abdillah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked us about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and later he married her mother. He said: 'There is no problem; she is not in the same position as a free woman, so do not contradict the earlier reports, because it is not explicit in the report that if he later marries her mother, it is permissible for him to have sexual relations with her. Rather, it implies that he may marry her mother. And we say that he may marry her with ownership and usage, but not sexual relations. And his saying, 'She is not in the position of a free woman,' means that this [slave] is not in the position of a free woman, because sexual relations are prohibited with a free woman except through the contract of marriage. This is not the case with a slave, because sexual relations are prohibited with a slave except through ownership, which is the cause for the permissibility of sexual relations in one of the states. Thus, the free woman is distinguished from the slave woman by this.'

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a man marrying the mother of his female slave after having relations with her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a man who has sexual relations with his female slave and later marries her mother faces no legal impediment, distinguishing the slave's status from that of a free woman. He explains that while a free woman requires a marriage contract (‘aqd) as the cause for permissibility, a slave woman’s permissibility is derived directly from ownership (milk), which remains valid even after her mother is married to the same master. This ruling highlights the distinct legal mechanisms governing concubinage versus marriage in Shia jurisprudence.
